rule: A Codex execution-rule file in the user layer is accepted by tools/adoption/codex_hook_trust.py without --allow-exec-rules only if its sha256 is on this list (and the conditions of its entry hold on this host) or it is Codex's own allow-only format. An entry is a review of one exact file: rtk's rewrite cannot take a command that a restricting rule of the file matches out of the rule's reach. Any edit to the file changes its hash and ends the review.

entries.name: hcom-deny.rules
entries.source: native-agent-stack #713, evidence/artifacts/new-wsl-install-plan-20261002/config/hcom-deny.rules at head 7fbe586f3 (repair round 2 narrowed the comments and the justification strings of 5f295f254's file, sha256 845f06b0ca31d03956df813ea7ab426e42ab784de7f39010c4a70cc91e3bc0e1; every other line, the patterns, decisions, match and not_match lists, is identical, checked by comparing the two files without their comment and justification lines); the copy kept for this review is evidence/artifacts/token-stack-fresh-session-e2e-20261004/fixtures/hcom-deny.rules

reviewed_for.rtk_configuration: the default hook configuration: [hooks].transparent_prefixes empty and no user TOML filters

entries.why: Every rule is a prefix rule on `hcom ...` or `uvx hcom ...`. rtk 0.51.0 rewrites a command only when its first word, after peeling env prefixes, global options, absolute paths and wrappers, is one of the heads derived from its source (evidence/artifacts/token-stack-fresh-session-e2e-20261004/rtk-rewrite-heads.json); neither `hcom` nor `uvx` is one, so no command that a rule of the file matches is rewritten; a command behind a wrapper (`time hcom ...`) is outside a prefix rule's reach with or without the rewrite.
